title: VITA: Zero-Shot Value Functions via Test-Time Adaptation of Vision–Language Models
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: A meta-learned adaptation module is trained once, then updates itself at test time to give zero-shot value estimates on unseen trajectories.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right, training vs inference, update equation under modules
description: Two stacked rounded panels, labeled (a) Training and (b) Inference. Each panel flows left to right. Panel (a) starts with a cylinder, the dataset, holding language instructions in purple banners and robot-manipulation frames. An arrow leads into an orange box with a blue frozen Vision-Language Encoder, a purple Adaptation Module and a pink Value Function Head. A red arrow loops back on the adaptation module. The update rule θ_t = θ_{t-1} − η∇ℓ_self(z_t; θ_{t-1}) sits under the modules. Red arrows carry the gradient of the prediction loss ℓ_pred from the head output back to the adaptation module and head. Panel (b) has the same pipeline. Its input is a cloth-folding instruction with three frames, and its output is the frames labeled 0%, 50% and 100% progress. Pastel fills and red accents guide the eye.
caption: Overview of VITA. VITA learns a goal-conditioned value function via meta-learning and achieves zero-shot generalization to out-of-distribution trajectories via test-time adaptation.
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show promise as zero-shot goal-conditioned value functions, but their frozen pre-trained representations limit generalization and temporal reasoning. We introduce VITA, a zero-shot value function learning method that enhances both capabilities via test-time adaptation. At inference, a lightweight adaptation module is updated via a gradient step on a meta-learned self-supervised loss, such that each test-time update improves value estimation. By updating sequentially over a trajectory, VITA encodes history into its parameters, addressing the temporal reasoning limitations. To mitigate shortcut learning, we propose a dissimilarity-based sampling strategy that selects semantically diverse segments of the trajectory during training. In real-world robotic manipulation tasks, VITA generalizes from a single training environment to diverse out-of-distribution tasks, environments, and embodiments, outperforming the state-of-the-art zero-shot method using autoregressive VLMs. Furthermore, we demonstrate that VITA's zero-shot value estimates can be utilized for reward shaping in offline reinforcement learning, resulting in multi-task policies on the Meta-World benchmark that exceed the performance of those trained with the simulation's fuzzy-logic dense rewards. Project website: https://chziakas.github.io/vita/.
